topics.name: Physical properties of metals and non-metals

questions.title: Which metal ignores cold water?
questions.text: Which one of the following metals does not react with cold water?
steps: ① K and Na react violently with cold water
② 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ (+ heat)
③ Ca reacts less violently: Ca(OH)₂ + H₂
④ Mg does not react with cold water
⑤ Mg reacts only with hot water
∴ Magnesium → (d)
questions.remember: Cold water: K, Na (violent), Ca (less violent). Hot water: Mg. Steam: Al, Zn, Fe. No reaction: Pb, Cu, Ag, Au.
questions.trap: Picking calcium: calcium DOES react with cold water, just less violently than sodium.
questions.tryit: Which metal reacts only with steam: Na, Ca or Fe?

questions.title: Why does magnesium float?
questions.text: When Mg metal is treated with hot water, it starts floating on the surface of the water. The reason for its different behaviour is:
opts: Mg is a lighter element than water.
Mg reacts with water to produce H₂ gas which helps in floating.
Mg reacts with water to produce N₂ gas which helps in floating.
Mg reacts with water to form CO₂ gas which helps in floating.
steps: ① Mg + hot water: a reaction starts
② Mg + 2H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ + H₂
③ H₂ bubbles stick to the metal surface
④ The bubbles lift the metal: it floats
∴ H₂ bubbles → (b)
questions.ans: Option (b) Mg reacts with water to produce H₂ gas, which helps in floating
questions.remember: Metal + water → metal hydroxide (or oxide) + hydrogen. Mg and Ca float because hydrogen bubbles stick to their surface.
questions.trap: Picking 'Mg is lighter than water': magnesium is denser than water; it floats only because of the H₂ bubbles.
questions.tryit: Which other metal floats in water for the same reason?

questions.title: The alloy with a non-metal
questions.text: Alloys are homogeneous mixtures of a metal with a metal or non-metal. Which among the following alloys contains a non-metal as one of its constituents?
steps: ① Brass = copper + zinc (both metals)
② Bronze = copper + tin (both metals)
③ Amalgam = mercury + another metal
④ Steel = iron + a little carbon
⑤ Carbon is a non-metal ✓
∴ Steel → (d)
questions.remember: Brass: Cu + Zn. Bronze: Cu + Sn. Solder: Pb + Sn. Amalgam: Hg + any metal. Steel: Fe + C (stainless steel adds Ni and Cr).
questions.trap: Picking amalgam: mercury is a liquid METAL, not a non-metal.
questions.tryit: Solder is an alloy of which two metals?

questions.title: Which pair gives hydrogen with dilute HCl?
questions.text: On reaction with dilute HCl, which of the following pairs of metals will evolve hydrogen gas?
steps: ① Only metals ABOVE hydrogen in the reactivity series displace it
② Cu and Ag are below hydrogen ⟹ no H₂
③ So (a), (b), (c) each contain a 'no' metal ✗
④ Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
⑤ 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂
∴ Magnesium and aluminium → (d)
questions.remember: Reactivity series: K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb [H] Cu Hg Ag Au. Metals above H give H₂ with dilute HCl; Cu, Hg, Ag, Au don't.
questions.trap: Picking a pair with copper or silver: both sit BELOW hydrogen, so even one of them makes the pair wrong.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 3 · Section 3.2.3 and the reactivity series (Table 3.2)
questions.tryit: Why is hydrogen gas not evolved when most metals react with nitric acid?
questions.tryans: HNO₃ is a strong oxidising agent: it oxidises H₂ to water

questions.title: Iron filings in four salt solutions
questions.text:
A student added iron filings to four test tubes A, B, C and D containing aqueous solutions of ZnSO₄, CuSO₄, FeSO₄ and Al₂(SO₄)₃ respectively.
(i) In which test tube will he observe the most vigorous reaction, and why?
(ii) Write a balanced equation for the reaction involved.
steps: ① A metal displaces only a LESS reactive metal
② A (ZnSO₄), D (Al₂(SO₄)₃): Zn, Al are more reactive than Fe ✗
③ C (FeSO₄): same metal, nothing to displace ✗
④ B (CuSO₄): Fe is more reactive than Cu ✓
⑤ Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu
∴ Test tube B: blue → pale green, brown Cu forms
questions.ans: (i) Test tube B: iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper · (ii) Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu
questions.remember: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution. Fe + CuSO₄: blue solution turns pale green; reddish-brown copper coats the iron.
questions.trap: Picking A or D because zinc and aluminium are 'strong': they are MORE reactive than iron, so iron can't displace them.
questions.tryit: Will copper displace silver from AgNO₃ solution?

questions.title: Give reasons: carbon, ionic compounds, solder
questions.text:
(a) Why can the oxides of highly reactive metals not be reduced by carbon?
(b) Why do ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points?
(c) Why is solder, an alloy of lead and tin, used for welding electrical wires together?
steps: ① (a) Na, Mg, Ca hold oxygen more strongly than carbon does
② So carbon can't pull O away; use electrolysis of molten chlorides
③ (b) Ions are held by strong electrostatic forces
④ A lot of energy is needed to break these forces
⑤ (c) Solder has a LOW melting point
⑥ It melts easily and joins wires without damage
∴ Stronger affinity · strong forces · low melting point
questions.ans: (a) They have more affinity for oxygen than carbon (extracted by electrolysis) · (b) Strong electrostatic forces between ions need much energy to break · (c) Solder has a low melting point
questions.remember: Top of the series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al): electrolysis of molten chlorides. Middle (Zn, Fe, Pb): reduce oxides with carbon. Bottom (Cu, Hg): heat alone.
questions.trap: (c): writing 'solder is a good conductor'. The marking point is its LOW MELTING POINT.
questions.tryit: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis and not by carbon?
questions.tryans: Aluminium has more affinity for oxygen than carbon

questions.title: MgO by electron transfer
questions.text:
(i) Write one example each of a metal that is so soft that it can be cut with a knife, and a non-metal that is a good conductor of electricity.
(ii) Using the electronic configuration, explain how a Mg atom combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide by transfer of electrons. [Atomic number: Mg = 12, O = 8]
steps: ① (i) Soft metal: sodium (or potassium)
② Non-metal that conducts: graphite (carbon)
⑤ Both reach a stable octet
⑥ Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ attract ⟹ Mg²⁺O²⁻ (MgO)
∴ Na · graphite · 2 electrons from Mg to O
questions.ans: (i) Sodium; graphite · (ii) Mg (2, 8, 2) loses 2e⁻ → Mg²⁺; O (2, 6) gains 2e⁻ → O²⁻; the ions attract to form Mg²⁺O²⁻
questions.remember: Metals lose electrons (cations), non-metals gain them (anions); the ions are held by electrostatic attraction: an ionic bond.
questions.trap: Drawing shared electrons (a covalent bond) for MgO. It's a TRANSFER: show the arrow from Mg to O and the charges.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 3 · Section 3.3.1 How do metals and non-metals react?
questions.tryit: Show the electron transfer in forming NaCl (Na = 11, Cl = 17).
questions.tryans: Na (2, 8, 1) loses 1e⁻ → Na⁺; Cl (2, 8, 7) gains it → Cl⁻
